title: perf(console): the first load no longer downloads spec schemas the Console never reads, nor the whole form package
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuJyLDyhPTFkFALvgwhFG59d)_

Part of #37444. Part of #37572. This is the first bytes cut of the first-screen card: it takes 97,612 gzipped bytes out of the Console's first load. Both cards stay open: the list page and the record page still miss the 2,500 ms line, and what keeps the rest of `@objectstack/spec` in the first load is schemas the Console really calls at runtime (listed under Acceptance notes), which needs narrower spec exports and is not this PR.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：所有用户打开控制台任意页面时，首屏要下载的脚本少了约 95 KB（gzip 后），首页和列表页更快一点；页面内容、行为都不变。
- 为什么做：属于「首屏 2.5 秒」卡的字节一刀（#37572）。HTTP/2 口径下各 10 次中位数（main → 本分支）：首页 2245 → 2172，列表页 2718 → 2652，记录页 2646 → 2640 毫秒；首页在 2.5 秒内，列表和记录页还没进线，所以这张卡和 #37444 都不关。
- 出错会怎样：spec 构建会把"没人读的模块级常量"交给打包器删掉。如果哪个常量在初始化时顺手往别处写东西，被删后那次写入就没了；这类写法已逐个查过并排除（13 处 `Object.assign(已有 schema, …)` 不包），另有测试扫描整个 spec 源码，出现新的"加载时注册"写法会红。改动可整笔撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。spec 路径会触发契约审核（L2），由座位安排。

## What changes

The first load (the chunks every Console page fetches before it can draw) measured 1,996,960 bytes gzipped across 124 chunks on `main` `ce4d8c7d`, and 1,899,348 across 123 on this branch's build commit `003fde60`:

| chunk | `ce4d8c7d` | `003fde60` | delta |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `vendor-objectstack` | 698,253 | 647,764 | −50,489 |
| `plugin-form` | 48,162 | — | −48,162 |
| everything else | 1,250,545 | 1,251,584 | +1,039 |
| aggregate | 1,996,960 | 1,899,348 | −97,612 |

- `packages/spec/tsup.config.ts`: a new pass, `wrapModuleScopeInitializers`, runs before the existing `annotatePureCalls` in both `onLoad` sites. It wraps each module-scope `const` / `let` initializer in a PURE-annotated arrow called at once, `/* @__PURE__ */ (() => (init))()`. A PURE annotation only covers the call it marks, not its arguments, receiver or chained calls, so a derived constant such as `new Set([...PageComponentType.options, ...Object.keys(ComponentPropsMap)])` was kept by every bundler, with every schema it names. Measured with rolldown 1.2.15 (the Console's bundler): a consumer importing only `resolveI18nLabel` kept 235 KB gzipped of spec before, under 1 KB after. Left unwrapped: initializers that are already trivially pure (literals, names, functions), a marked constructor call whose arguments are trivially pure (its own annotation covers it), and every initializer that hands `Object.assign` / `Object.defineProperty` / `Object.defineProperties` / `Object.setPrototypeOf` / `Reflect.*` an object it did not create. Function bodies are not touched.
- `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`: `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES` is built from a plain list of names, `TRANSLATED_METADATA_TYPE_NAMES`, instead of `Object.keys(METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS)`, so the Console's metadata client reading the set no longer keeps every translator and the schemas they read. The translator table now `satisfies` a record keyed by exactly those names, so a translator without its name, or a name without a translator, fails the type check. The exported type (`ReadonlySet<string>`) and its members are unchanged.
- `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/core.ts`: re-exports `createKeepsField` from the side-effect-free `@object-ui/plugin-form/core`. That is one new export on a published subpath (the package root already exports it; nothing is removed or renamed), and it is the widening the `Clause-②` line names. `@objectstack/spec`'s public surface does not change.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx`: imports `createKeepsField` from `@object-ui/plugin-form/core` instead of the package root, which kept the whole `plugin-form` group eager. `ui/apps/console/vite.config.ts` adds `createKeepsField` to the `plugin-form-core` group's module list.
- `ui/scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`: the aggregate ceiling is re-pinned from 2,489,948 to 2,407,237, lowered by exactly what the closure lost between the previous `BASELINE` (`cc378e93`, 1,982,059) and `003fde60`, so the headroom stays 507,889 bytes (0.71x the regression line), as the objectstack#25925 entry did. `BASELINE` moves to `003fde60`. The four per-chunk rows did not move (`vendor-objectstack` 647,764 under 842,730, 0.27x). The unit test's rendered literal moves from `1935.6` to `1854.8`.

No behaviour, string, route or saved document changes. Changeset: `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@object-ui/plugin-form`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/console` and `@objectstack/console` (the Console's chunk rules and the dist it ships change).

## What was checked for the module-scope wrapping, and what was found

Wrapping an initializer tells the bundler it has no side effects. That is false for an initializer that writes to something that outlives it, so the spec sources were searched for two kinds of write:

1. **An initializer that writes into an existing object.** Found 13, all `export const X = Object.assign(XSchema, { create })` (`api/endpoint.zod.ts` 1, `api/documentation.zod.ts` 3, `api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts` 2, `api/rest-server.zod.ts` 2, `system/worker.zod.ts` 4, `system/http-server.zod.ts` 1). Dropping one would remove `create` from the schema itself. The pass detects the whole family (the `MUTATES_FIRST_ARGUMENT` set) and leaves them unwrapped; a test pins `Object.assign(TaskSchema, …)` and `Object.defineProperty(Target, …)` as untouched while `Object.assign({}, …)` and `Object.freeze(Object.keys(…))` are wrapped.
2. **An initializer that registers into a store other code reads later.** Two families do, and both are wrapped because dropping one loses nothing a reader can ask for (the first contract-review round found both; the first version of this PR missed them):
   - `withRefusalHead(prescription, head)`, 6 constants in `data/query.zod.ts`, puts a refusal constant's one-line head in a process-wide map on `globalThis`. Only code that raises that same constant reads the map, and that code reads the constant, so a bundle that can raise the text keeps the initializer that registered it.
   - Every strict object (`strictObject`, `strictObjectError` and the schema helpers built on them) pushes its declaration into a process-wide store. Only this package's tests and `scripts/build-schemas.ts` read it, and they load the sources, never a bundle.

   `packages/spec/scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts` holds this account in two cases. The first lists every module-level store a function writes (by name, through a member chain, a type-only cast, `globalThis`, or a module-level function's result such as `registry().set(…)`), 39 entries, each with its reason, and marks the five that are registrations (the two above and the three runtime `registerMetadataType*` overlays). The second reads every module-scope initializer (over 1,000 load-time calls) and refuses one whose load-time calls reach a registration store, directly or through the functions they call (matched by name), by a name that store's reason does not cover. Ablation: a module-scope `registerMetadataTypeSchema('probe', z.string())` reds it with `registerMetadataTypeSchema → kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts EXTRA_METADATA_TYPE_SCHEMAS`. A positive control pins the reach on a fixture. Calls are matched by name, not resolved, and a helper that writes only to its own parameter is not a store, so this guards the known shapes rather than proving the absence of every one; the `wrapModuleScopeInitializers` docblock says the same.

## Tests

- `packages/spec/scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts`: 15 tests, 15 passed. New cases: what is wrapped and what is not (literals, marked constructors with pure arguments, the `Object.assign` family, function bodies), the order of the two passes (wrap then annotate, no double annotation), a bundled fixture consumer (an unused derived constant drops its schema; the control that reads it keeps it), the module-state ledger, the load-time registration reach and its positive control.
- Spec: `tsc --noEmit`, `check:scripts-typecheck`, `check:test-typecheck` exit 0; `vitest run src/system/i18n* src/data/picklist.test.ts` and the pure-construction test: 20 files, 807 tests passed (at `c840b723`).
- UI: `pluginCoreSubpaths-33581.test.ts` and `side-effects-declaration-consistency.test.ts`: 126 passed; `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 in `ui/packages/plugin-form` and `ui/packages/app-shell`; `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts`: 174 passed; `pnpm check:eager-closure` on the branch build: pass (aggregate 0.71x, every per-chunk row in range, chunk membership exact).

## Acceptance notes

- **Measured effect** — production build (`pnpm console:build`), `objectstack start` with `NODE_ENV=production`, behind a local HTTP/2 TLS front (the card's acceptance condition, #37444 ruling 7205984444), Lighthouse 13.6.0 desktop preset, headless Chrome, signed in, cold cache. Two rounds of five runs per page and build, the second round in reverse order (branch first), so each figure is a median of 10:

  | Page | h2 `main` `ce4d8c7d` | h2 this branch | delta | script KB |
  |:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
  | Home | 2245 | 2172 | −73 | 1924 → 1832 |
  | Object list | 2718.5 | 2652 | −66 | 2276 → 2231 |
  | Record page | 2646 | 2640.5 | −5 | 2180 → 2135 |

  Every report's `finalUrl` is the page asked for (home, `showcase_task` list, a `showcase_task` record). Every `https:` Script request in all 60 reports went over `h2` (main 1570 / 2460 / 1940, branch 1560 / 2470 / 1950 requests per page over 10 reports). The HTTP/1.1 control was not re-run for this change. Home stays under 2500 ms; the list page misses by 152 ms and the record page by 141 ms. The record page's gain is inside its noise (each build's 10 runs spread about 200 ms): it needed the form package's code later in its load anyway.
- **What still holds spec in the first load** (per-name measurement against this build: for each spec name an eager module imports, the gzipped bytes only that name keeps): `ActionSchema` (31.7 KB, `actionDialogCompanion.ts` safeParses an action's `preflight`), `FieldSchema` (28.4 KB, `reference-keys.ts` reads its key set), `ListViewSchema` (22.9 KB, `userFilterUrlState.ts` reads `.shape.sort`), `ManifestSchema` (13.2 KB, `packages-io.ts` reads `.shape.id`), `FormViewSchema` (11.0 KB, `submitRedirect.ts` safeParses a `submitBehavior`), `DashboardSchema` (7.9 KB). Each reads one sub-schema of a large one; exporting those sub-schemas from spec would let the Console drop the rest, but that is a public spec API addition and a separate change.
- L2 owed (not self-reviewed): `packages/spec/**` is a contract path.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `cd packages/spec && pnpm exec vitest run --project local scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts` → 15 passed.

Read first: `wrapModuleScopeInitializers` and `writesToAnExistingObject` in `packages/spec/tsup.config.ts` (what is excluded from wrapping is the whole safety argument), then `MODULE_STATE_WRITTEN_IN_FUNCTIONS`, `REGISTRATION_STORES` and `LOAD_TIME_REGISTRATIONS` in the test.

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes. (eslint over the changed files: 0 errors; the warnings in `RelatedRecordActionsBridge.tsx` predate this change, which edits one import line there)

- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
